verifications.claim: Lightning occurs typically during thunderstorms.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Lightning is usually associated with cumulonimbus clouds (thunderclouds) (R3); The most common occurrence of a lightning event is known as a thunderstorm (R5); Lightning is the most spectacular element of a thunderstorm (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state lightning is typically or most commonly associated with thunderstorms.

verifications.claim: Lightning occurs during volcanic eruptions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: sometimes in the dust and gases emitted by erupting volcanoes (R3); volcanic lightning, which can occur during volcanic eruptions (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention volcanic lightning during eruptions.

verifications.claim: Lightning occurs during intense forest fires.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Lightning can also occur during dust storms, forest fires... Intense forest fires... can produce lightning (also called Fire Lightning) (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Wikipedia directly states lightning occurs during intense forest fires.

verifications.claim: Lightning occurs during nuclear explosions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Thermonuclear explosions... have been seen triggering lightning flashes... large nuclear explosions may develop... clear-air lightning discharges (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for lightning triggered by nuclear explosions.

verifications.claim: Lightning produces a bright flash of light (visible radiation).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: There is an emission of electromagnetic radiation across a wide range of wavelengths, some visible as a bright flash (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Explicit description of visible bright flash from lightning.

verifications.claim: Lightning produces thunder (the sound of the air rapidly expanding).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The heated air expands explosively, creating a shockwave... heard as thunder (R1); Thunder is produced by rapid heating of the air... expand at supersonic speeds (R3); air to expand explosively fast... shock wave that turns into... thunder (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm thunder from rapid air expansion due to lightning heat.

verifications.claim: Lightning strikes Earth roughly 44 (± 5) times per second.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: lightning on Earth occurs at an average frequency of approximately 44 (± 5) times per second (R5)

verifications.claim: Lightning totals nearly 1.4 billion flashes annually.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: equating to nearly 1.4 billion flashes per year (R5)

verifications.claim: The air around a lightning bolt can reach temperatures of up to 30,000°C (54,000°F).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: as hot as 54,000 °F (30,000 °C) (R1); peak temperatures... 30,000 °C (50,000 °F) (R3); heats to temperatures of about 30,000 °C (54,000 °F) (R5)

verifications.claim: 30,000°C is five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: That's five times hotter than the surface of the Sun! (R1)

verifications.claim: The return stroke (the bright flash) travels at about 100,000 km/s.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The rate at which the return stroke current travels has been found to be around 100,000 km/s (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact speed and attribution to return stroke.

verifications.claim: 100,000 km/s is roughly one-third the speed of light.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: at a speed about one-third the speed of light (R3); 100,000 km/s (one-third of the speed of light) (R5)

verifications.claim: An average bolt carries about 30,000 amperes (30 kA) of current.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: peak currents in return strokes to negative leaders are typically about 30,000 amperes (R3); An average bolt of negative lightning creates an electric current of 30,000 amperes (30 kA) (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match for average bolt current.

verifications.claim: An average bolt transfers 15 coulombs of charge.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: transferring a total 15 C (coulombs) of electric charge (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match for average negative bolt.

verifications.claim: Megaflashes travel over 100 km (62 miles) horizontally.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: a megaflash as "a continuous mesoscale lightning flash with a horizontal path length of approximately 100 km or greater." (R5)

verifications.claim: A record-breaking flash in 2017 stretched 829 km (515 miles) across Texas and Kansas.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the longest observed flash occurred in October 2017 across Texas and Kansas, measuring 829 km (515 mi) (R5)

verifications.claim: Intra-cloud (IC) lightning is the most common type.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: IC lightning is the most frequently occurring type (R5); roughly 5 to 10 times as many flashes that remain in the cloud (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm IC as most common.

verifications.claim: Intra-cloud (IC) lightning occurs within a single thundercloud.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Intra-cloud (IC) or in-cloud – Within a single thundercloud (R5)

verifications.claim: Cloud-to-cloud (CC) lightning consists of discharges between two different clouds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Cloud-to-cloud (CC) or inter-cloud – Between two clouds (R5)

verifications.claim: Cloud-to-ground (CG) lightning is a discharge between a cloud and the ground.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Cloud-to-ground (CG) – Between a cloud and the ground (R5)

verifications.claim: Cloud-to-ground (CG) lightning is the most dangerous type.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: it poses the greatest threat to life and property (R5); cloud-to-ground lightning can be more dangerous and even deadly (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Sources state CG is most dangerous to humans/property.

verifications.claim: Lightning forms when warm, moist air mixes with colder air, creating atmospheric disturbances that polarize the air.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Lightning primarily occurs when warm air is mixed with colder air masses, resulting in atmospheric disturbances necessary for polarizing the atmosphere (R5)

verifications.claim: Rapidly rising and falling air inside a storm causes water droplets and ice particles to collide, leading to charge separation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Winds inside the cloud are very turbulent... updrafts... downdrafts... ice going down meets the water coming up (R1); rising ice crystals collide with graupel (R5); ice crystals... crash into each other (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Describes collision mechanism via air movements.

verifications.claim: Charge separation typically creates a negative charge at the base of the cloud.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: a cloud with a negatively charged bottom (R1); middle to the lower part of the thunderstorm cloud becomes negatively charged (R5); the middle and lower part of the storm to become negatively charged (R10)

verifications.claim: Charge separation typically creates a positive charge at the top of the cloud.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: a positively charged top (R1); upper part of the thunderstorm cloud becomes positively charged (R5); top of the thunderstorm cloud to become positively charged (R10)

verifications.claim: A stepped leader of negative charge descends from the cloud in a zigzagging, invisible path.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "stepped leader" of negative charge descends from the cloud (R1); stepped leader... propagates downward... highly branched (R3); channel of negative charges called a stepped leader makes its path... in a series of steps (R11)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe negative stepped leader as zigzagging/invisible.

verifications.claim: As the negative leader nears the ground, positive charges from the ground reach up, usually from tall, conductive objects.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: a positive charge, called a streamer, reaches up... tallest objects like trees, telephone poles (R1); upward, connecting discharge... from grounded objects (R3); currents of positive charges called streamers or upward leaders start moving upward from the ground, usually along elevated objects (R11)

verifications.claim: When the leader and streamer meet, a powerful electric current flows, creating the brilliant, visible flash.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: The channels connect and we see the lightning stroke (R1); When the junction is complete... very bright return stroke (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Describes connection leading to visible return stroke.

verifications.claim: Lightning often strikes outside the rain area.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Lightning can strike where it’s not raining (R6); Lightning can strike outward 10 miles from a thunderstorm (R10)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm strikes outside rain area.

verifications.claim: Lightning strikes as far as 10 miles (16 km) from the thunderstorm.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: lightning can strike outward 10 miles from a thunderstorm (R10)

verifications.claim: The National Weather Service advises, "When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors!".
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: When thunder roars, go indoors! (R1); When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors (R6)

verifications.claim: Substantial buildings with plumbing/wiring are considered safe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: go inside an enclosed building... stay away from... showers, sinks... electronic equipment (R1); Move immediately to safe shelter -- a building (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Enclosed buildings with plumbing/wiring implied safe if precautions followed.

verifications.claim: Fully enclosed metal-topped vehicles are considered safe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: fairly safe in a vehicle, if the windows are up and you do not touch any metal (R1); inside a closed metal topped vehicle with the windows up (R2)

verifications.claim: Sheds are not considered safe.

verifications.evidence: No relevant content found

verifications.claim: Picnic shelters are not considered safe.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.evidence: No relevant content found
verifications.reasoning: No mention of picnic shelters in any provided references.

verifications.claim: 90% of people struck by lightning survive.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: 90 percent of people struck by lightning survive (R5); Only about 10%... are killed, leaving 90% (R8)

verifications.claim: Sheet lightning is a cloud illuminated from within, with the bolt itself hidden.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "sheet lightning"... observer may see only a flash of light (R5); sheet lightning is used to describe an IC flash embedded within a cloud that lights up as a sheet of luminosity (R9)

verifications.claim: Heat lightning is a distant flash seen on a hot night, with no audible thunder.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "heat lightning", which can be seen from a great distance but not heard (R5); heat lightning, is any lightning... too far away for the thunder to be heard (R9)
verifications.reasoning: Direct definition, 'hot night' implied by term.

verifications.claim: Ball lightning is often described as a floating sphere of light.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: ball lightning, which is rarely observed (R5); floating sphere of lightning, usually between 1 centimeter and 1 meter (R7)

verifications.claim: Sprites and jets are Transient Luminous Events occurring high above thunderstorms, such as red sprites, blue jets, and elves.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: transient luminous events (TLEs)... red sprites, blue jets, and elves (R9); elves, sprites and blue jets (R11)
